sources.sentence: The decision is not as cut and dried as it first appears.

brief.meaningEn: Clearly settled or straightforward, with little room for doubt or debate.
brief.meaningZh: 清楚確定或直接了當，沒有多少疑問或爭議空間。
brief.grammar: be/seem cut and dried; often not as cut and dried as it seems; cut-and-dried before a noun.
brief.register: Common idiom, especially in negative statements about complex decisions.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是說事情已完成，也不是所有人感受相同；否定句常提醒有未考慮的複雜處。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要留意 not：not cut and dried 表示並非那麼簡單確定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提醒決策有多個相關因素，而非草率說已有唯一答案。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看這個選擇？

options.en: It needs more consideration than the price alone suggests.
options.zh: 它需要比只看價錢更多的考慮。

options.en: It has one obvious answer with no trade-offs.
options.zh: 它只有一個明顯答案，沒有取捨。

options.en: It has already been made and cannot be discussed.
options.zh: 它已經決定，不能再討論。

options.en: The cheaper course has more practice sessions.
options.zh: 較便宜的課程有更多練習次數。

listening.explanationZh: not 和練習較少指出價格以外的取捨；不是已作最終決定。
listening.en: The choice is not as cut and dried as it seems: the cheaper course has fewer practice sessions.
listening.zh: 選擇並非表面上那麼簡單確定：較便宜的課程練習次數較少。

reply.promptEn: Should we simply choose the cheapest venue?
reply.promptZh: 我們是否直接選最便宜的場地就可以？

options.en: We need to check whether everyone can reach it easily.
options.zh: 我們要查大家是否容易到達。

options.en: It is not cut and dried; the travel costs may change the comparison.
options.zh: 事情並非簡單確定；交通費可能改變比較結果。

options.en: The hire fee is only one part of the total cost.
options.zh: 租金只是總費用的一部分。

options.en: Let us compare the facilities before making a decision.
options.zh: 我們先比較設施，再決定吧。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都合理提醒不要只看租金；金句明示未能輕率下結論。

scene.promptZh: 兩個方案一個快但昂貴，一個便宜但需要更多人手，你還未知道人手是否足夠。哪句合適？

options.en: The decision is not cut and dried; we need to check our staffing.
options.zh: 決定並非簡單確定；我們要查人手。

options.en: There is no relevant difference between the plans.
options.zh: 兩個方案沒有任何相關分別。

options.en: The decision is already final, so staffing cannot matter.
options.zh: 決定已經落實，所以人手不可能重要。

scene.explanationZh: 費用、時間及人手有取捨，不能說沒有分別或已定案。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 not cut and dried？

options.en: The issue may involve relevant complications.
options.zh: 事情可能有相關的複雜因素。

options.en: Further information could affect the decision.
options.zh: 更多資料可能影響決定。

options.en: The answer is necessarily obvious and beyond discussion.
options.zh: 答案必定明顯，沒有討論空間。

contrast.explanationZh: 否定句是指出不那麼簡單確定，並非肯定唯一明顯答案。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你說不簡單，就是永遠不能決定了吧？」哪句較準確？

options.en: It is not cut and dried, but checking the key details should help us decide.
options.zh: 事情並非簡單確定，但查清主要細節應能幫我們決定。

options.en: Decide from the first available figure and leave the missing details until later.
options.zh: 按首個已有數字決定，把欠缺細節留待之後。

options.en: Keep collecting details without deciding which ones could affect the choice.
options.zh: 一直收集細節，卻不判斷哪些會影響選擇。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認有取捨後，應查會影響決定的主要細節，不是忽略欠缺資料，也不是漫無目標地一直收集。

speaking.en: The answer is not cut and dried, so let us check the details first.
speaking.zh: 答案並非簡單確定，所以我們先查細節吧。
speaking.promptZh: 你想在決定前提醒大家考慮相關細節。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你比較兩份兼職，一份工資較高但交通時間很長，另一份近家但工資較低。用一至兩句英文說明需要考慮取捨。

examples.en: The choice is not cut and dried. I need to compare the travel time as well as the pay.
examples.zh: 選擇並非簡單確定。我除了工資，也要比較交通時間。

examples.en: It is not cut and dried because the better-paid job involves a long journey. I should work out the total time and cost.
examples.zh: 事情並非簡單確定，因為較高薪的工作需要長途交通。我應算清總時間和費用。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留 not，指出交通與工資的具體取捨；不要把複雜當成永遠無法決定。

takeaways.en: The situation is not as cut and dried as the headline suggests.
takeaways.zh: 情況並非標題所示那麼簡單確定。

takeaways.en: It seemed cut and dried until we checked the missing information.
takeaways.zh: 我們查到缺少的資料之前，事情看來簡單確定。

lessons.titleEn: stuck in the same old box

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The course is no longer stuck in quite the same old box.
sources.expression: stuck in quite the same old box

brief.meaningEn: Restricted by an established category or way of thinking.
brief.meaningZh: 受既有分類或思考方式限制。
brief.grammar: be stuck in the same old box; source quite is optional emphasis, not a necessary part of the metaphor.
brief.register: Creative container metaphor; name the limiting category or assumption.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是固定慣用語的必背長句，也不是任何熟悉方法都不好；需有實際限制。
brief.misconceptionZh: no longer stuck 表示已開始突破，不能漏讀否定而說仍然受困。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出舊框架的具體限制及新的可能做法。

options.en: It now allows formats beyond the previous narrow category.
options.zh: 它現在容許原先狹窄分類以外的形式。

options.en: It still permits only the previous essay format.
options.zh: 它仍只容許原有文章形式。

options.en: It has stopped offering students any project choices.
options.zh: 它已不再提供任何項目選擇。

options.en: It has removed every written assignment from the course.
options.zh: 它把所有書面作業從課程刪掉。

listening.explanationZh: no longer 與 beyond written essays 說明擴大選擇，不是完全禁止文章。
listening.en: The course is no longer stuck in the same old box; students can now choose projects beyond written essays.
listening.zh: 課程不再困在舊框架；學生現在可以選擇書面文章以外的項目。

reply.promptEn: Why are you changing the way students can present their research?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼改變學生展示研究的方式？

options.en: An essay is useful, but it should not be the only option.
options.zh: 文章有用，但不應是唯一選項。

options.en: We do not want the project stuck in the same old box.
options.zh: 我們不想項目困在舊框架。

options.en: Audio interviews could reveal details that a report alone might miss.
options.zh: 錄音訪問可能呈現單靠報告看不到的細節。

options.en: Different formats give students more ways to explain their findings.
options.zh: 不同形式讓學生有更多方法解釋發現。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都合理支持擴大研究展示形式；金句描述框架限制，不否定文章本身。

scene.promptZh: 社團一直只把攝影視為記錄活動，現在想讓成員用照片講故事，但仍有人拒絕考慮這種用法。哪句描述後者最貼切？

options.en: Their thinking is stuck in the same old box.
options.zh: 他們的想法困在舊框架。

options.en: They have already welcomed every proposed new use.
options.zh: 他們已歡迎每種新建議用法。

options.en: Their options are limited by a lack of camera equipment rather than an established way of thinking.
options.zh: 他們的選項受相機器材不足限制，而非既有思考方式。

scene.explanationZh: 拒絕考慮攝影的其他用途，顯示想法困在舊分類；題設並非器材不足，也未接受新方向。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 stuck in the same old box 得出？

options.en: An established assumption may be limiting the choices considered.
options.zh: 既有假設可能限制考慮的選項。

options.en: Every familiar method must be useless and should be banned.
options.zh: 每種熟悉方法都必定沒用，應被禁止。

options.en: A different perspective could reveal another possibility.
options.zh: 不同角度可帶來另一可能。

contrast.explanationZh: 批評限制不等於全盤否定熟悉方法；要看任務需要。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「要跳出舊框架，就必須禁止寫文章。」哪句較準確？

options.en: We can avoid being stuck in the same old box by adding choices, not banning a useful format.
options.zh: 我們可增加選項，避免困在舊框架，而不用禁止有用形式。

options.en: Keep the essay-only rule until everyone has agreed how all the new formats should be assessed.
options.zh: 等所有人同意怎樣評估全部新形式後，才改只准文章的規則。

options.en: Replace the essay-only rule with an audio-only rule for the next projects.
options.zh: 把接下來項目只准文章的規則，換成只准錄音。

dialogue.explanationZh: 擴大選擇可保留文章並逐步加入適合形式，不用換成另一個單一形式，也不用等所有形式評估完才嘗試。

speaking.en: Our thinking is no longer stuck in the same old box.
speaking.zh: 我們的想法不再困在舊框架。
speaking.promptZh: 你看到小組開始考慮新形式。先聽，再說，留意 no longer。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：閱讀社過去只接受書面書評，現在想加錄音分享，但有人以為這代表書評再沒價值。用一至兩句英文說明改變。

examples.en: The club is no longer stuck in the same old box. Audio discussions can sit alongside written reviews.
examples.zh: 社團不再困在舊框架。錄音討論可以和書面書評並存。

examples.en: We do not need to stay stuck in the same old box; adding audio gives readers another way to share ideas.
examples.zh: 我們不用一直困在舊框架；加錄音讓讀者有另一方法分享想法。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明新增錄音選擇及書評仍可有價值；保留句中否定或 no longer 的意思。

takeaways.en: The project need not remain stuck in the same old box.
takeaways.zh: 項目不必一直困在舊框架。

takeaways.en: We were stuck in the same old box until we considered a different format.
takeaways.zh: 我們考慮另一種形式前，一直困在舊框架。

sources.sentence: Fashion is a moving target for retailers.

brief.meaningEn: A goal, standard or situation that keeps changing, making a response harder to plan.
brief.meaningZh: 不斷改變的目標、標準或情況，令規劃應對較難。
brief.grammar: a moving target; requirements/prices/preferences can become a moving target.
brief.register: Common figurative expression in planning and evaluation.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課不是實際移動的靶；改變帶來規劃難度，不等於永遠無法應對。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要有前後改變的證據，不只因目標困難便叫 moving target。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪項標準在改變，以及如何追蹤或協調更新。

listening.promptZh: 設計小組面對甚麼困難？

options.en: The conditions kept changing as they tried to meet them.
options.zh: 他們嘗試達標時，條件仍不斷改變。

options.en: The conditions were difficult but unchanged throughout.
options.zh: 條件很難，但從頭到尾沒有改變。

options.en: The client accepted the first design without changes.
options.zh: 客戶接受了首個設計，沒有改動。

options.en: The team had already agreed a final stable set of conditions.
options.zh: 小組已同意一套最終穩定條件。

listening.explanationZh: every time 和 different condition 顯示反覆改變，不只是固定而困難。
listening.en: The requirements became a moving target: every time we revised the design, the client added a different condition.
listening.zh: 要求變成不斷改變的目標：每次修改設計，客戶都加上另一條件。

reply.promptEn: Why is it hard to finish the event poster?
reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼難以完成活動海報？

options.en: The venue details change whenever we prepare a draft.
options.zh: 每次我們準備草稿，場地資料都變。

options.en: The brief has become a moving target, so we need to confirm the final details.
options.zh: 要求變成不斷改變的目標，所以要確認最終細節。

options.en: We keep receiving a new version of the schedule after making edits.
options.zh: 我們每次改好，又收到新版時間表。

options.en: No one has yet confirmed which date should appear on the final copy.
options.zh: 還沒有人確認定稿應寫哪個日期。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均實際解釋海報難完成；金句指出反覆改變及所需確認。

scene.promptZh: 每次你調整網站以符合規則，規則就在未通知下再改，小組難以知道哪版才有效。哪句合適？

options.en: The rules have become a moving target.
options.zh: 規則變成不斷改變的目標。

options.en: The rules stayed identical throughout the project.
options.zh: 規則在整個項目都完全相同。

options.en: The team finished before any rules were issued.
options.zh: 小組在任何規則發出前已完成。

scene.explanationZh: 反覆更新規則並欠通知造成變動目標，不是固定或事前完成。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜稱為 a moving target？

options.en: Requirements change during each round of revisions.
options.zh: 要求在每輪修改都改變。

options.en: A difficult standard remains clearly defined and unchanged.
options.zh: 困難的標準一直清楚確定，沒有改變。

options.en: Customer preferences keep shifting during a long development process.
options.zh: 顧客偏好在漫長開發期間不斷轉變。

contrast.explanationZh: 困難本身不是變動；固定而清楚的標準缺少 moving 的重點。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「條件會變，那就永遠不用追蹤了吧？」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: If the brief is a moving target, we need a clear way to record and confirm changes.
options.zh: 如果要求不斷改變，我們需要清楚方法記錄及確認更新。

options.en: Keep editing from whichever version each volunteer received first.
options.zh: 繼續按每位義工最早收到的版本修改。

options.en: Wait for the next change without recording which earlier condition it replaces.
options.zh: 等下一次更改，卻不記錄它取代哪項舊條件。

dialogue.explanationZh: 變動要求需要一致有效版本及更新紀錄；各用舊版或不記錄替代關係，都容易再做錯。

speaking.en: The schedule is a moving target, so we should confirm the latest version.
speaking.zh: 時間表不斷改變，所以我們應確認最新版本。
speaking.promptZh: 你想提醒小組確認有效資料。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社團展覽的場地、日期已改了幾次，你每次做好宣傳又要重做。用一至兩句英文描述問題，並建議先確認資料。

examples.en: The exhibition plans have become a moving target. Let us confirm the venue and date before printing more posters.
examples.zh: 展覽計劃變成不斷改變的目標。我們先確認場地日期，再印更多海報吧。

examples.en: The schedule is a moving target, so we need one agreed update that everyone can check before sharing it.
examples.zh: 時間表不斷改變，所以我們需要一個大家同意的更新版本，讓每個人分享前都可查閱。

glossary.zh: 一個大家同意的更新版本

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出場地或日期反覆變動，提出確認版本；不要只說目標困難或完全不能應對。

takeaways.en: The requirements became a moving target during development.
takeaways.zh: 開發期間，要求變成不斷改變的目標。

takeaways.en: When prices are a moving target, check the latest figures before deciding.
takeaways.zh: 價格不斷變動時，決定前先查最新數字。

sources.sentence: Small firms are often lighter on their feet.

brief.meaningEn: Able to react and adapt quickly, especially when compared with a less flexible organisation.
brief.meaningZh: 能迅速反應和調整，尤其用於比較組織的靈活程度。
brief.grammar: be light/lighter on one’s feet; this lesson teaches organisational agility, not literal dancing or balance.
brief.register: Conversational business metaphor; use evidence of quick adaptation.
brief.boundaryZh: 規模小不保證靈活，規模大也不必然遲鈍；比較的是反應方式，不是體重。
brief.misconceptionZh: 快不等於不用檢查或計劃，應交代如何安全而有效調整。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體反應速度說明靈活，而不作規模偏見。

options.en: The team adapted its process quickly after feedback.
options.zh: 小組收到回饋後迅速調整流程。

options.en: The team refused to change its established process.
options.zh: 小組拒絕改變既有流程。

options.en: The team waited until the problem disappeared without action.
options.zh: 小組不作處理，等問題自行消失。

options.en: The team changed the process before hearing any feedback.
options.zh: 小組在聽到任何回饋前已改流程。

listening.explanationZh: 收到問題後一天內調整，是迅速反應的證據；不是不變或等候。
listening.en: The small team was lighter on its feet: it changed the booking process within a day when users reported a problem.
listening.zh: 小組反應較靈活：使用者反映問題後，一天內就改好預約流程。

reply.promptEn: How did your group respond when the venue became unavailable?
reply.promptZh: 場地不能使用時，你們小組怎樣應對？

options.en: We checked two alternatives and confirmed a new room that afternoon.
options.zh: 我們查了兩個替代選擇，當天下午就確認新房間。

options.en: We were light on our feet and moved the session online after checking everyone could join.
options.zh: 我們靈活應變，確認大家能參加後，把活動改為網上進行。

options.en: The organiser contacted us quickly and agreed a backup plan.
options.zh: 主辦方迅速聯絡我們，並同意後備方案。

options.en: We adjusted the programme so the smaller room could still work.
options.zh: 我們調整流程，令較小房間仍能使用。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述實際應對場地問題；金句保留確認可參與的檢查，而非倉促亂改。

scene.promptZh: 兩間機構收到相同預約問題，一間先試後備流程並當天修正，另一間一星期後才開始討論。哪句最有根據？

options.en: The first organisation was lighter on its feet in this case.
options.zh: 在這次情況，第一間機構反應較靈活。

options.en: The second organisation changed its process first.
options.zh: 第二間機構先改流程。

options.en: The first organisation mainly waited for the other one to act.
options.zh: 第一間機構主要等待另一間先行動。

scene.explanationZh: 第一間當天試流程及修正，支持這次反應較靈活；不是第二間先改，或第一間等待對方。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜單憑 lighter on their feet 作出？

options.en: They adapted more quickly in the situation described.
options.zh: 他們在所述情況調整得更快。

options.en: Their response suggests flexibility.
options.zh: 他們的回應顯示靈活。

options.en: They never need planning or checks before changing a process.
options.zh: 他們改流程前永遠不用計劃或檢查。

contrast.explanationZh: 靈活不免除合適計劃與檢查，迅速與審慎可並存。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我們人少，所以必定比所有大機構靈活。」哪句較準確？

options.en: We may be lighter on our feet, but we need to judge that by how we respond, not size alone.
options.zh: 我們可能反應較靈活，但應看實際應對方式，而不只看規模。

options.en: Compare only the headcounts without checking recent response times.
options.zh: 只比較人數，不查最近的回應時間。

options.en: Assume the larger branch will need a week and do not ask about its current process.
options.zh: 假設較大分部需要一星期，不問目前流程。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應按實際應對速度及做法比較靈活程度，不能只看人數或未查流程便推斷大分部較慢。

speaking.en: We need to be light on our feet without skipping the necessary checks.
speaking.zh: 我們要靈活應變，同時不省略必要檢查。
speaking.promptZh: 你想同時強調應變及審慎。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：活動當天突然下雨，你們迅速改用室內空間，先確認通道安全及參加者都收到通知。用一至兩句英文描述應變。

examples.en: Our team was light on our feet when the rain started. We checked the indoor space and quickly informed the participants.
examples.zh: 下雨時，小組靈活應變。我們檢查室內空間，並迅速通知參加者。

examples.en: We were lighter on our feet than last time because we already had a safe backup room and a contact list.
examples.zh: 因為已有安全的後備房間和聯絡名單，我們這次比上次應變更靈活。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用迅速換地方及通知支持靈活，並保留安全檢查；比較句需有上次或另一對象作基準。

takeaways.en: A clear backup plan can help a team stay light on their feet.
takeaways.zh: 清楚後備方案可幫小組保持靈活應變。

takeaways.en: The smaller unit was lighter on its feet during the changeover.
takeaways.zh: 轉換期間，較小的單位反應更靈活。

sources.sentence: The large group has the financial muscle to expand.

brief.meaningEn: The financial resources or spending power to carry out a substantial plan.
brief.meaningZh: 有足夠金錢資源或投資能力，推行規模較大的計劃。
brief.grammar: have/lack/build the financial muscle to + verb; muscle is metaphorical strength.
brief.register: Common business metaphor; not a guarantee of success or moral superiority.
brief.boundaryZh: 有財力不表示每項計劃都合理、資金無限或一定成功；缺資金也不等於想法差。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應把金錢能力與技術、需求及執行能力分開。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋資金對計劃的作用，同時指出其他所需因素。

options.en: Enough financial resources for the equipment purchase.
options.zh: 足夠購買器材的金錢資源。

options.en: A guarantee that the equipment would solve every problem.
options.zh: 器材能解決所有問題的保證。

options.en: All the trained staff required to use the equipment.
options.zh: 使用器材所需的所有受訓員工。

options.en: A reason to abandon the equipment purchase for lack of money.
options.zh: 因缺錢而放棄購買器材的理由。

listening.explanationZh: 財力支持購買，但 but 後明確保留員工技能的需要。
listening.en: The company had the financial muscle to buy new equipment, but it still needed staff who could use it well.
listening.zh: 公司有財力買新器材，但仍需要懂得妥善使用的員工。

reply.promptEn: How can the larger organisation afford several new centres?
reply.promptZh: 較大的機構為甚麼負擔得起幾個新中心？

options.en: It has built up substantial reserves for expansion.
options.zh: 它為擴展累積了大量儲備。

options.en: It has the financial muscle to fund the buildings.
options.zh: 它有財力為建築工程提供資金。

options.en: Long-term donors have committed money to the project.
options.zh: 長期捐款者已承諾資助項目。

options.en: Its approved budget covers the planned sites.
options.zh: 已批准預算足以支付計劃中的場地。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋可負擔擴展的金錢來源或能力；金句不保證營運成功。

scene.promptZh: 小型製作室設計出好方案，但沒足夠資金購買所需機器。哪句最準確？

options.en: It lacks the financial muscle to buy the machines at present.
options.zh: 它目前缺乏購買機器的財力。

options.en: The studio rejected the machines because the design no longer needs them.
options.zh: 製作室因設計不再需要那些機器而拒絕購買。

options.en: It already has enough money for every planned purchase.
options.zh: 它已有足夠金錢支付所有計劃購買。

scene.explanationZh: 問題是目前資金不足，並非設計不需要機器，也不是已有足夠預算。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 financial muscle 作出？

options.en: An organisation can fund a substantial purchase.
options.zh: 機構有能力資助一項大額購買。

options.en: Its financial resources guarantee that every expansion will succeed.
options.zh: 它的財力保證每次擴展都成功。

options.en: Money may allow an option that a smaller budget cannot support.
options.zh: 金錢可能讓一項較小預算無法支持的選項成為可能。

contrast.explanationZh: 資金能力與最終成效不同；仍需技能及合適計劃。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「他們有錢買器材，就不用培訓人員了。」哪句最準確？

options.en: Financial muscle can fund the equipment, but training is still necessary to use it effectively.
options.zh: 財力可支付器材，但有效使用仍需要培訓。

options.en: Order the equipment now and postpone planning operator training until it arrives.
options.zh: 現在先訂器材，等到貨才規劃操作員培訓。

options.en: Choose the most expensive machine before asking what the staff need to learn.
options.zh: 未問員工要學甚麼，便選最貴機器。

dialogue.explanationZh: 有財力仍需在採購前考慮使用技能及培訓；只看最貴或到貨才規劃，都未處理人員需要。

speaking.en: They have the financial muscle to invest, but they still need a workable plan.
speaking.zh: 他們有財力投資，但仍需要可行計劃。
speaking.promptZh: 你想同時承認財力及計劃需要。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區劇團想升級燈光，但現有預算不足，打算先尋找資助及確認培訓需要。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: The theatre group lacks the financial muscle to replace the lights now. We need funding and a training plan.
examples.zh: 劇團目前缺乏更換燈光的財力。我們需要資助及培訓計劃。

examples.en: A sponsor could give us the financial muscle to upgrade the lighting, but we would still need trained operators.
examples.zh: 贊助者可讓我們有財力升級燈光，但我們仍需要受訓操作員。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說清資金不足或可能資助，以及培訓需求；不用把資金當成成功保證。

takeaways.en: The group has the financial muscle to open another branch.
takeaways.zh: 這個集團有財力再開一間分店。

takeaways.en: Financial muscle alone cannot replace careful planning.
takeaways.zh: 單有財力不能代替審慎規劃。

sources.sentence: The company offers a clear career ladder.

brief.meaningEn: A sequence of jobs or levels through which someone can advance in their working life.
brief.meaningZh: 工作生涯中可逐步晉升的一連串職位或級別。
brief.grammar: climb/move up the career ladder; a step on the career ladder.
brief.register: Common work-life metaphor; one model of progress, not the only successful career path.
brief.boundaryZh: 有晉升路徑不保證自動升職，也不是所有工作都按直線級別發展。
brief.misconceptionZh: 技能成長或轉行也可有價值，不必把職位愈高等同人愈有價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認晉升機會與保證之別，並按個人目標比較路徑。

options.en: A possible route through more senior roles, with conditions attached.
options.zh: 一條可能晉升較高職位的路徑，仍有條件。

options.en: An automatic promotion on a fixed date for every trainee.
options.zh: 每位見習員都會在固定日期自動升職。

options.en: A promise that no additional skills will be needed.
options.zh: 保證不用學額外技能。

options.en: A timetable covering only the initial assistant training, with no later roles described.
options.zh: 時間表只涵蓋初期助理培訓，沒有提及之後職位。

listening.explanationZh: from assistant to team leader 提供級別，but 後保留技能和空缺條件。
listening.en: The firm showed trainees a career ladder from assistant to team leader, but each promotion depended on skills and available roles.
listening.zh: 公司向見習員展示從助理到組長的晉升階梯，但每次升職仍取決於技能及職位空缺。

reply.promptEn: What attracts you to this training programme?
reply.promptZh: 這個培訓計劃甚麼地方吸引你？

options.en: It explains the skills needed for more responsible roles.
options.zh: 它說明擔任責任較大職位所需的技能。

options.en: There is a clear career ladder, so I can understand the possible next steps.
options.zh: 它有清楚職涯階梯，讓我了解可能的下一步。

options.en: The mentors help trainees plan their development.
options.zh: 導師幫見習員規劃發展。

options.en: I can see how the initial tasks connect to later opportunities.
options.zh: 我看得出最初工作如何連結日後機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述發展方面的吸引力；金句不聲稱晉升必定發生。

scene.promptZh: 公司列明初級設計師、設計師及主管的責任和申請條件，員工可按條件申請下一級。哪句合適？

options.en: The company sets out a career ladder for designers.
options.zh: 公司列明設計師的職涯晉升階梯。

options.en: The company accepts only outside applicants and offers no internal route between the levels.
options.zh: 公司只接受外來申請者，不提供內部逐級申請的路徑。

options.en: The company has no distinction between the roles.
options.zh: 公司沒有區分那些職位。

scene.explanationZh: 不同職位、條件及逐級申請構成職涯階梯；不是只准外來招聘，也不是職位沒分別。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 a career ladder 得出？

options.en: There may be a sequence of roles with greater responsibility.
options.zh: 可能有一系列責任逐步增加的職位。

options.en: People can investigate the requirements for a next role.
options.zh: 人們可了解下一職位的要求。

options.en: Everyone who starts at the bottom is guaranteed to reach the top.
options.zh: 每個從基層開始的人都保證能升到最高層。

contrast.explanationZh: 路徑存在不等於所有人必定完成每個級別。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「不想當主管，就是不想進步吧？」哪句較合理？

options.en: The career ladder is one route, but developing specialist skills can also be valuable.
options.zh: 職涯階梯是一條路，但發展專門技能也有價值。

options.en: Treat a management title as better development without asking what skills the job involves.
options.zh: 不問工作涉及甚麼技能，就把管理職銜當成更好的發展。

options.en: Turn down the specialist course because it does not lead to a management post.
options.zh: 因專才課程不通往管理職位，便拒絕參加。

dialogue.explanationZh: 晉升管理只是發展路徑之一；應看實際技能及個人目標，不只按職銜或是否做主管判斷。

speaking.en: I want to understand the career ladder before choosing the programme.
speaking.zh: 選這個計劃前，我想了解職涯晉升階梯。
speaking.promptZh: 你想了解發展路徑再作選擇。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你考慮加入維修公司，想知道從學徒到技師再到培訓員，需要甚麼技能及空缺。用一至兩句英文提出查詢。

examples.en: I would like to understand the career ladder from apprentice to trainer. What skills and vacancies affect each step?
examples.zh: 我想了解從學徒到培訓員的職涯階梯。每一步取決於甚麼技能和空缺？

examples.en: Could you explain the career ladder and the requirements for becoming a technician? I know promotion is not automatic.
examples.zh: 你可以解釋職涯階梯及成為技師的要求嗎？我知道升職不是自動的。

writing.selfCheckZh: 具體查詢職位之間的要求，不把清楚路徑當成自動升職承諾。

takeaways.en: The programme explains the first steps on the career ladder.
takeaways.zh: 計劃解釋職涯晉升階梯的最初幾步。

takeaways.en: Moving up the career ladder may require new skills and an available role.
takeaways.zh: 沿職涯階梯晉升，可能需要新技能及職位空缺。

lessons.titleEn: a small cog in a very big machine

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: He felt like a small cog in a very big machine.
sources.expression: a small cog in a very big machine

brief.meaningEn: A person with a small role in a large organisation, often feeling little influence over the whole.
brief.meaningZh: 在大型機構中角色很小的一員，常帶有覺得難以影響整體的感受。
brief.grammar: feel like/be a small cog in a (very) big machine; often describes personal experience.
brief.register: Common organisation-as-machine image; may sound self-deprecating.
brief.boundaryZh: 職責小不表示人沒價值，也不保證每個大機構都令人疏離；要交代感受或影響範圍。
brief.misconceptionZh: 描述的是組織角色或感受，不是建議把人當可隨便替換的機件。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述有限影響的感受，並提出了解或參與流程的下一步。

options.en: Their narrow role left them feeling disconnected from the bigger purpose.
options.zh: 狹窄職責令他們感到與整體目的脫節。

options.en: They personally controlled every decision in the project.
options.zh: 他們親自控制項目中的每個決定。

options.en: They had already understood how every team worked together.
options.zh: 他們已了解每個小組如何合作。

options.en: They had been told that their form was the only important part.
options.zh: 他們被告知那份表格是唯一重要部分。

listening.explanationZh: 看不到工作與整體連結，解釋渺小及脫節感；不是掌握全部決策。
listening.en: I felt like a small cog in a very big machine because I handled one form each day but never saw how it helped the wider project.
listening.zh: 我覺得自己像大機構中渺小的一員，因為每天只處理一份表格，卻看不到它如何幫助整個項目。

reply.promptEn: Why do you feel disconnected from the larger project?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼覺得與整個項目脫節？

options.en: I only see my small task and rarely hear what happens afterwards.
options.zh: 我只看見自己的小任務，很少知道之後怎樣。

options.en: I feel like a small cog in a big machine, without a clear view of the wider purpose.
options.zh: 我像大機構中渺小的一員，看不清整體目的。

options.en: Decisions are made elsewhere and no one explains how our work fits in.
options.zh: 決定由其他地方作，沒有人解釋我們的工作如何配合。

options.en: I would feel more involved if I could understand the other teams’ work.
options.zh: 如果能了解其他小組的工作，我會更有參與感。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明脫節原因或所缺連結；金句描述感受，不否定個人價值。

scene.promptZh: 你只負責錄入一類資料，從未聽到整體項目進展，覺得無法影響決策。哪句合適？

options.en: I feel like a small cog in a big machine.
options.zh: 我覺得自己像大機構中渺小的一員。

options.en: I make every major decision for the whole project.
options.zh: 我為整個項目作每個重大決定。

options.en: I have a complete view of how all the teams cooperate.
options.zh: 我完全了解所有小組如何合作。

scene.explanationZh: 有限職責及看不到全局，支持小角色的感受；不是決策者或全知。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜從 small cog in a big machine 得出？

options.en: The person may feel their influence is limited.
options.zh: 那個人可能覺得影響有限。

options.en: The person has no value and can never contribute anything useful.
options.zh: 那個人沒有價值，永遠不能作有用貢獻。

options.en: Their role is a small part of a much larger organisation.
options.zh: 他們的角色是大機構的一小部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 小角色或有限影響，不代表人無價值或貢獻無用。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你只是其中一小部分，那工作肯定沒用。」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: I may feel like a small cog in a big machine, but I can ask how my work supports the whole project.
options.zh: 我可能覺得自己像大機構中渺小的一員，但可問自己的工作如何支持整個項目。

options.en: Stop checking your entries carefully until someone offers a more visible role.
options.zh: 等有人提供較受注意的崗位，才仔細檢查自己的輸入資料。

options.en: Ask to switch tasks immediately without finding out how the present work is used.
options.zh: 不先了解目前工作的用途，便立即要求換任務。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先了解工作與整體連結，可回應脫節感；降低仔細程度或未查用途就換任務，都未處理對貢獻的疑問。

speaking.en: I felt like a small cog in a big machine until someone explained the wider purpose.
speaking.zh: 有人解釋整體目的前，我一直覺得自己像大機構中渺小的一員。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述了解全局前的脫節感。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在大型活動只負責掃描門票，不知道入場資料之後怎樣使用，覺得與其他小組脫節。用一至兩句英文描述感受並提出查詢。

examples.en: I feel like a small cog in a big machine when I only scan tickets. Could someone explain how the entry data helps the organisers?
examples.zh: 我只掃描門票時，覺得像大機構中渺小的一員。有人可以解釋入場資料如何幫助主辦者嗎？

examples.en: Scanning tickets makes me feel like a small cog in a very big machine, so I would like to learn how our team supports the event.
examples.zh: 掃描門票令我覺得像大機構中渺小的一員，所以想了解我們小組如何支持活動。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出脫節感及想了解的具體連結，不說小職責等於人或工作沒價值。

takeaways.en: He felt like a small cog in a big machine before meeting the other teams.
takeaways.zh: 認識其他小組前，他覺得像大機構中渺小的一員。

takeaways.en: Being a small cog in a very big machine does not make your contribution worthless.
takeaways.zh: 身為大機構中一小部分，不代表你的貢獻毫無價值。

sources.sentence: The studio has a close-knit team.

brief.meaningEn: Connected by strong personal relationships, with frequent contact or mutual support.
brief.meaningZh: 人與人關係緊密，常有聯繫或互相支持。
brief.grammar: a close-knit family/community/team; hyphenated compound adjective.
brief.register: Common descriptive English; not a guarantee that everyone agrees.
brief.boundaryZh: 成員不必有血緣或永不爭論；關係緊密也不必排斥新加入的人。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只看成員人數，需有持續交流、關心或互助線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體互助行為描述緊密群體，並容許意見不同。

listening.promptZh: 甚麼支持 close-knit 的描述？

options.en: Ongoing personal contact and mutual support.
options.zh: 持續的人際聯繫及互相支持。

options.en: A guarantee that every member agrees on every question.
options.zh: 每位成員對每個問題都同意的保證。

options.en: A rule preventing new members from joining.
options.zh: 禁止新人加入的規定。

options.en: A lack of contact outside formal instructions.
options.zh: 除了正式指示外沒有聯繫。

listening.explanationZh: 關心及互助顯示緊密關係；沒有全體同意或封閉成員規定。
listening.en: The workshop had a close-knit team: members checked on one another and shared help during busy weeks.
listening.zh: 工作坊的小組關係緊密：成員互相關心，在忙碌星期分擔幫忙。

reply.promptEn: What makes you enjoy volunteering with this group?
reply.promptZh: 這個小組甚麼地方令你喜歡在這裏做義工？

options.en: People notice when someone needs help and offer it without fuss.
options.zh: 大家會留意誰需要幫忙，並自然伸出援手。

options.en: It is a close-knit group where members support one another.
options.zh: 這個小組關係緊密，成員互相支持。

options.en: I have regular conversations with people who remember how I am doing.
options.zh: 我常跟關心我近況的人聊天。

options.en: I feel comfortable asking the others for advice.
options.zh: 我很放心向其他人請教。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述群體關係的正面經驗；金句不要求血緣或完全同意。

scene.promptZh: 街坊經常互相照應、幫忙取藥及分享消息，即使住在不同大樓也很熟悉。哪句合適？

options.en: They are a close-knit community.
options.zh: 他們是一個關係緊密的社區。

options.en: They know little about one another and never offer help.
options.zh: 他們互不熟悉，也從不幫忙。

options.en: They must all belong to the same family.
options.zh: 他們必定全都屬於同一家人。

scene.explanationZh: 持續關心及互助支持社區緊密，不要求住同樓或有血緣。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜單憑 close-knit 作出？

options.en: The members maintain strong relationships.
options.zh: 成員保持緊密關係。

options.en: The members can rely on one another for support.
options.zh: 成員可互相依靠尋求支持。

options.en: Members never disagree and cannot welcome outsiders.
options.zh: 成員永不爭論，也不能歡迎外人。

contrast.explanationZh: 緊密不是全無分歧，也不是必然排外。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我們有不同意見，便不能說關係緊密吧？」哪句較準確？

options.en: A close-knit team can disagree while still listening and supporting one another.
options.zh: 關係緊密的小組可以有分歧，同時仍聆聽及互相支持。

options.en: Avoid raising the disagreement so the group can look united.
options.zh: 不提分歧，讓小組看來團結。

options.en: Ask the member with a different view to sit out the discussion.
options.zh: 請持不同看法的成員不要參與討論。

dialogue.explanationZh: 緊密關係可以容許尊重地討論分歧，不需隱藏問題或排除不同意見的成員。

speaking.en: We are a close-knit team, even when we have different ideas.
speaking.zh: 即使有不同想法，我們仍是關係緊密的小組。
speaking.promptZh: 你想同時表達緊密關係及容許分歧。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的園藝社成員常互相照顧植物、分享工具，也會耐心帶新手參與。用一至兩句英文描述群體關係。

examples.en: Our gardening club is a close-knit group. Members share tools and help beginners care for their plants.
examples.zh: 園藝社是一個關係緊密的小組。成員分享工具，幫新手照顧植物。

examples.en: We have a close-knit community that welcomes newcomers and checks on members who need help.
examples.zh: 我們是一個關係緊密的社區，歡迎新人，也關心需要幫助的成員。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用分享工具、照料植物及帶新手等行為支持關係緊密，不需要聲稱人人想法相同。

takeaways.en: The close-knit community welcomed the new residents.
takeaways.zh: 關係緊密的社區歡迎新居民。

takeaways.en: A close-knit team can discuss disagreements respectfully.
takeaways.zh: 關係緊密的小組可以尊重地討論分歧。

sources.sentence: The proposal began to take shape after the meeting.

brief.meaningEn: Begin to develop a recognisable form or clearer structure.
brief.meaningZh: 開始有可辨認的樣貌或較清楚的結構。
brief.grammar: an idea/plan/project takes shape; began to take shape; has taken shape.
brief.register: Common figurative expression for development; also has literal uses.
brief.boundaryZh: 成形不表示已完成或不需修改；要有由模糊變清楚的過程。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把開始有結構誤當成已實行或成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述構思如何變清楚，並指出仍待完成的工作。

options.en: It began to have a clearer structure.
options.zh: 它開始有較清楚的結構。

options.en: The exhibition had already opened to visitors.
options.zh: 展覽已經向觀眾開放。

options.en: The team had abandoned every idea.
options.zh: 小組已放棄所有想法。

options.en: The timetable guaranteed that no changes would be needed.
options.zh: 時間表保證不用任何修改。

listening.explanationZh: 整理和草擬令計劃變清楚，不是活動已開幕或完全不能修改。
listening.en: After we grouped the ideas and sketched a timetable, the exhibition plan began to take shape.
listening.zh: 我們整理想法並草擬時間表後，展覽計劃開始成形。

reply.promptEn: How is the community workshop plan going?
reply.promptZh: 社區工作坊計劃進行得怎樣？

options.en: We have agreed the main activities and are working on the timings.
options.zh: 我們已同意主要活動，正處理時間安排。

options.en: It is starting to take shape now that we have a clear audience and a rough programme.
options.zh: 有了清楚對象及初步流程，計劃現在開始成形。

options.en: The first outline is ready, though we still need to confirm the venue.
options.zh: 首份大綱已好，但還要確認場地。

options.en: We have turned the initial ideas into a more organised proposal.
options.zh: 我們把最初想法整理成較有條理的建議書。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述計劃逐漸清楚的進展；金句不聲稱所有安排已落實。

scene.promptZh: 你們起初只有零散點子，討論後已列出主要部分及次序，但還要查預算。哪句合適？

options.en: The proposal is beginning to take shape.
options.zh: 建議書開始成形。

options.en: The whole project is finished and all costs are confirmed.
options.zh: 整個項目已完成，所有費用已確認。

options.en: The discussion left the ideas no clearer than before.
options.zh: 討論後，想法仍和以前一樣不清楚。

scene.explanationZh: 主要部分與次序開始明確就是成形；預算尚待處理。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 take shape 作出？

options.en: An idea is becoming more clearly organised.
options.zh: 一個想法正變得更有條理。

options.en: The plan is necessarily finished, approved and ready to launch.
options.zh: 計劃必定已完成、獲批，並可立即推出。

options.en: A previously vague proposal is gaining a recognisable structure.
options.zh: 原先模糊的建議正有可辨認的結構。

contrast.explanationZh: 開始成形不是完成、批准或推出的保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「計劃有樣子了，那不用再查預算吧？」哪句較合理？

options.en: It is taking shape, but we still need to check the budget before committing.
options.zh: 計劃正在成形，但承諾推行前仍要查預算。

options.en: Book the largest room now and check whether the budget covers it afterwards.
options.zh: 先訂最大房間，之後才查預算能否支付。

options.en: Reject the whole proposal before asking whether a smaller version is affordable.
options.zh: 未問較小版本是否負擔得起，便否決整份建議。

dialogue.explanationZh: 成形後仍須查預算，可按資料調整規模；先承諾大場地或未問便全盤否決，都不是妥善處理。

speaking.en: The plan is taking shape, but the budget still needs work.
speaking.zh: 計劃正在成形，但預算仍需處理。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述進展，同時保留未完成項目。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們已把校園展覽的零散點子整理成三個主題區，也畫了初步平面圖，但場地還未確認。用一至兩句英文報告進展。

examples.en: The exhibition is starting to take shape with three themed areas and a rough floor plan. We still need to confirm the venue.
examples.zh: 展覽有了三個主題區及初步平面圖，開始成形。我們仍需確認場地。

examples.en: Our ideas have taken shape in an initial layout, but the venue arrangements are not final yet.
examples.zh: 我們的想法已在初步佈局中成形，但場地安排仍未落實。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出主題區或平面圖提供了清楚結構，也保留場地未定；不要把成形當作已開幕。

takeaways.en: The proposal began to take shape after the group organised its ideas.
takeaways.zh: 小組整理想法後，建議書開始成形。

takeaways.en: A plan can take shape before every detail is settled.
takeaways.zh: 所有細節落實前，計劃已可以開始成形。

sources.sentence: Building a reputation is like a marathon.

brief.meaningEn: Requiring sustained effort over a long period rather than one short burst.
brief.meaningZh: 需要長期持續投入，而非一次短時間衝刺。
brief.grammar: X is/feels like a marathon; simile with like, not necessarily a fixed description of every long task.
brief.register: Common endurance comparison; pace and recovery may matter.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必真的跑步，也不表示必定痛苦或只能很慢；重點是長期持續。
brief.misconceptionZh: 持續投入不是永不休息，要安排可維持的節奏及階段目標。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述長期目標所需的持續投入和合理節奏。

options.en: Steady effort sustained over a long period.
options.zh: 長期持續而穩定的投入。

options.en: One intense afternoon was enough to learn every skill.
options.zh: 一個密集下午已足夠學會所有技巧。

options.en: Regular practice was less useful than avoiding the task.
options.zh: 定期練習不及避開任務有用。

options.en: The speaker had to finish within a single short deadline.
options.zh: 說話者必須在單一短限期內完成。

listening.explanationZh: several years 與 regular sessions 支持長期投入，不是一次短衝刺。
listening.en: Learning to restore old furniture is like a marathon: short, regular sessions have helped me improve over several years.
listening.zh: 學修復舊家具像長跑：幾年來，短而定期的練習幫我進步。

reply.promptEn: How do you plan to develop your drawing over the next few years?
reply.promptZh: 未來幾年，你打算怎樣提升繪畫？

options.en: I will practise regularly and review a small set of goals each month.
options.zh: 我會定期練習，每月檢討一小組目標。

options.en: It is like a marathon, so I need a pace I can sustain.
options.zh: 它像長跑，所以我需要能持續的節奏。

options.en: Short sessions will help me keep learning alongside schoolwork.
options.zh: 短時間練習可幫我兼顧功課，持續學習。

options.en: I want to build the habit gradually rather than do everything in one weekend.
options.zh: 我想逐步養成習慣，而不是一個週末做完所有事情。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出長期發展方法；金句把重點放在可持續節奏。

scene.promptZh: 義工正在整理多年檔案，需要按月逐批處理及檢查，預計持續一年。哪句合適？

options.en: The project is like a marathon, requiring steady work over many months.
options.zh: 項目像長跑，需要幾個月持續穩定工作。

options.en: The project needs only one short burst before lunch.
options.zh: 項目只需午飯前短時間衝刺。

options.en: The volunteers plan to leave all the sorting until one final afternoon.
options.zh: 義工打算把全部整理留到最後一個下午。

scene.explanationZh: 一年內逐月處理支持長期穩定投入，不是午飯前一次做完或把工作全留到最後一個下午。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 like a marathon 的工作比喻得出？

options.en: A sustainable pace can support a long-term effort.
options.zh: 可維持的節奏可支持長期投入。

options.en: Progress may require repeated work over time.
options.zh: 進步可能需要一段時間反覆投入。

options.en: Success requires working without any rest until the task ends.
options.zh: 成功要求工作到結束都不能休息。

contrast.explanationZh: 長期投入通常需要節奏及恢復，比喻不要求永不休息。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「目標要幾年，是否每晚都應做到很晚？」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: It is like a marathon; regular practice and enough rest are more sustainable than exhausting yourself each night.
options.zh: 它像長跑；定期練習和足夠休息，比每晚耗盡自己更能持續。

options.en: Double each evening session this week before checking whether that pace fits your work and rest.
options.zh: 未查能否兼顧工作及休息，就在本週把每晚練習加倍。

options.en: Wait for a completely free month before beginning, rather than trying a manageable weekly routine now.
options.zh: 等一個完全空閒的月份才開始，而非現在嘗試可維持的每週習慣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 長期目標需要可維持的節奏；未評估就加倍，或等完全空閒才開始，都沒有先建立合適規律。

speaking.en: The project feels like a marathon, so we need a sustainable pace.
speaking.zh: 項目感覺像長跑，所以需要可維持的節奏。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說明長期工作需要節奏。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想用一年整理家族舊照片，每週只有少量時間。用一至兩句英文說明長期投入及可維持的安排。

examples.en: Sorting the family photos is like a marathon. I will work on one small batch each week.
examples.zh: 整理家族照片像長跑。我會每週處理一小批。

examples.en: This project feels like a marathon, so I will make steady progress with short sessions and clear labels.
examples.zh: 項目感覺像長跑，所以我會用短時間工作和清楚標籤，穩定推進。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出長期整理及小批定期安排；不把長期投入寫成永不休息或一次完成。

takeaways.en: Building trust is like a marathon, not a single impressive performance.
takeaways.zh: 建立信任像長跑，不是一次令人印象深刻的表現。

takeaways.en: The restoration felt like a marathon, and regular breaks helped us continue.
takeaways.zh: 修復工作感覺像長跑，定期休息幫我們繼續。

sources.sentence: A small launch can feel like a sprint.

brief.meaningEn: Requiring a short period of fast, concentrated effort.
brief.meaningZh: 需要在短時間內快速集中投入。
brief.grammar: X feels/is like a sprint; a comparison to a short race, not necessarily technical project-management terminology.
brief.register: Common intensity-and-duration comparison.
brief.boundaryZh: 短期集中不表示省略檢查，也不宜把整個長期工作都當成不停衝刺。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可集中完成有界線的任務，但要有準備及之後恢復，不能靠匆忙保證品質。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分短期密集工作與長期持續目標。

options.en: A brief period of concentrated, fast work.
options.zh: 一段短時間的快速集中工作。

options.en: The whole project taking place at the same pace for several years.
options.zh: 整個項目幾年來都以相同速度進行。

options.en: The team abandoning the final checks to finish early.
options.zh: 小組放棄最後檢查，以提早完成。

options.en: A long pause before starting any preparation.
options.zh: 開始任何準備前的長時間停頓。

listening.explanationZh: final hour 及具體檢查安排支持短時密集投入，不是取消檢查。
listening.en: The final hour before the exhibition opened felt like a sprint as we checked labels and put the last displays in place.
listening.zh: 展覽開幕前最後一小時像短跑衝刺，我們集中檢查標籤並放好最後展品。

reply.promptEn: How did the last stage of packing the donation boxes feel?
reply.promptZh: 收拾捐贈箱的最後階段感覺怎樣？

options.en: We worked quickly together to finish the labelled boxes before collection.
options.zh: 我們一起快速工作，在收貨前完成貼好標籤的箱子。

options.en: It felt like a sprint, with everyone focused for that final half-hour.
options.zh: 它感覺像短跑衝刺，最後半小時大家都很專注。

options.en: The short deadline made the final stage intense.
options.zh: 短限期令最後階段很緊湊。

options.en: We concentrated on the remaining boxes and checked them as we went.
options.zh: 我們集中處理剩下箱子，同時邊做邊檢查。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均回答最後階段的密集感受；金句同時表達短時間與集中投入。

scene.promptZh: 校報小組已準備好文章，截稿前半小時集中核對姓名和版面後交稿。哪句合適？

options.en: The final check felt like a sprint.
options.zh: 最後檢查感覺像短跑衝刺。

options.en: The final check was spread evenly over the next year.
options.zh: 最後檢查平均分布在接下來一年。

options.en: They chose speed by leaving every name unchecked.
options.zh: 他們為快而完全不查姓名。

scene.explanationZh: 半小時集中核對支持短時衝刺，而非一年分布或省略檢查。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 like a sprint 的工作比喻得出？

options.en: The period involved fast and focused effort.
options.zh: 那段時間需要快速專注投入。

options.en: Important checks should be skipped because the work is short.
options.zh: 因為時間短，就應省略重要檢查。

options.en: The intensity was limited to a relatively short period.
options.zh: 密集程度集中在相對短的時段。

contrast.explanationZh: 短時密集不取消品質檢查；比喻說的是時間和強度。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「最後半小時要衝刺，那姓名不用核對了吧？」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: It may feel like a sprint, but checking the names is still part of finishing properly.
options.zh: 最後階段可能像短跑衝刺，但核對姓名仍是妥善完成的一部分。

options.en: Submit the draft now and leave the known name errors for readers to find.
options.zh: 現在交草稿，把已知姓名錯誤留給讀者發現。

options.en: Spend the remaining time changing the cover colour instead of checking names.
options.zh: 用剩下時間改封面顏色，不查姓名。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把必要檢查納入短時集中工作，不能以速度排除已知重要問題。

speaking.en: The last half-hour felt like a sprint, but we still checked the details.
speaking.zh: 最後半小時感覺像短跑衝刺，但我們仍核對了細節。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述最後階段密集，同時有做好檢查。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：義賣前最後二十分鐘，你們集中放好價錢牌並檢查找續金額。用一至兩句英文描述這段密集工作及檢查。

examples.en: The last twenty minutes felt like a sprint. We put out the price labels and checked the change together.
examples.zh: 最後二十分鐘感覺像短跑衝刺。我們一起放好價錢牌，核對找續。

examples.en: Setting up just before the sale was like a sprint, but we kept a checklist so the important details were not missed.
examples.zh: 義賣前佈置像短跑衝刺，但我們用清單，免得漏掉重要細節。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出短時間及集中工作的具體安排，不用把快等同跳過檢查。

takeaways.en: The final preparations felt like a sprint after weeks of planning.
takeaways.zh: 幾星期規劃後，最後準備感覺像短跑衝刺。

takeaways.en: A short task can feel like a sprint without replacing the need for care.
takeaways.zh: 短任務可以像衝刺，同時仍須細心。

lessons.titleEn: building the plane while flying it

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The new charity felt as if it was building the plane while flying it.
sources.expression: building the plane while flying it

brief.meaningEn: Develop the necessary systems while the activity is already operating.
brief.meaningZh: 活動已開始運作，同時仍在建立所需制度或工具。
brief.grammar: feel like/be building the plane while flying it; a vivid established metaphor, not literal aviation advice.
brief.register: Informal expression for work under uncertainty; often conveys pressure and risk.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是所有準備都沒有，也不表示做法值得模仿；仍須先有基本安全及責任安排。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應指出哪些部分邊做邊建，以及如何降低混亂，而非把欠準備當成英勇。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述營運與開發重疊的情況，並提出穩定流程的措施。

listening.promptZh: 這個比喻描述甚麼重疊？

options.en: Running the activity while still developing a system it needed.
options.zh: 活動運作期間仍在開發所需系統。

options.en: Finishing every system before the club welcomed anyone.
options.zh: 社團接待任何人前已完成所有系統。

options.en: Stopping all activity until no further changes were possible.
options.zh: 停止所有活動，直到完全不會再有改動。

options.en: Revising a closed project after its final session had ended.
options.zh: 最後活動結束後，才修改已關閉項目。

listening.explanationZh: already opened 和 still creating 說明運作與建立系統同時發生。
listening.en: We were building the plane while flying it: the reading club had already opened while we were still creating the booking system.
listening.zh: 我們像一邊飛一邊造飛機：閱讀社已開放，但我們仍在建立預約系統。

reply.promptEn: Why did the first month of the new club feel so demanding?
reply.promptZh: 新社團第一個月為甚麼感覺那麼吃力？

options.en: We were welcoming members while still working out the sign-up process.
options.zh: 我們接待新成員時，仍在整理報名流程。

options.en: We were building the plane while flying it, with the club running before every system was ready.
options.zh: 我們像一邊飛一邊造飛機，社團運作時，並非所有系統都準備好。

options.en: Each session revealed a missing procedure that we had to write before the next one.
options.zh: 每次活動都顯出欠缺的程序，我們要在下次前補寫。

options.en: The same people had to handle bookings and develop the new forms.
options.zh: 同一批人既要處理預約，也要開發新表格。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋營運與建立流程重疊造成的負擔；金句不是說所有準備都沒有。

scene.promptZh: 社區借物服務已每週開放，義工一邊處理借還，一邊補建紀錄工具。哪句合適？

options.en: They are building the plane while flying it.
options.zh: 他們正一邊運作，一邊建構所需系統。

options.en: Every tool was completed and tested before the service opened.
options.zh: 服務開放前，每個工具都已完成及測試。

options.en: They are only reviewing an old service that has stopped operating.
options.zh: 他們只在檢討一項已停止運作的舊服務。

scene.explanationZh: 借還正在進行，紀錄工具仍在建立，構成同時運作及開發。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 building the plane while flying it 得出？

options.en: Some development overlaps with an activity already in operation.
options.zh: 某些開發與已運作的活動重疊。

options.en: The team may face pressure from handling both tasks.
options.zh: 小組可能因同時處理兩項工作而受壓。

options.en: Essential safety checks can be ignored whenever a team is new.
options.zh: 只要小組是新的，就可忽略必要安全檢查。

contrast.explanationZh: 比喻描述壓力或未完成系統，不是免除基本安全責任。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然邊做邊建，我們就不用寫臨時流程吧？」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: We may be building the plane while flying it, but a clear temporary process will help us work safely and consistently.
options.zh: 我們可能正邊運作邊建構，但清楚臨時流程可幫大家安全而一致地工作。

options.en: Let each volunteer invent a different booking rule at every session.
options.zh: 讓每位義工每次活動都自訂不同預約規則。

options.en: Keep opening more sessions before assigning anyone to finish the missing procedures.
options.zh: 未安排人完成缺少的程序，便繼續加開活動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 臨時一致流程及責任分配可減少混亂；不能把比喻當成不用規劃的理由。

speaking.en: It felt as if we were building the plane while flying it, so we agreed a temporary process.
speaking.zh: 我們感覺像一邊運作一邊建構，所以議定了臨時流程。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述運作及開發同時進行，並交代穩定措施。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的社團已開始每週交換書本，但借還紀錄仍在製作。你們決定先用同一份表格並安排專人整理。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: We are building the plane while flying it because the book exchange is running before the records are complete. For now, we will use one shared form.
examples.zh: 我們正一邊運作一邊建構，因為交換書本已開始，紀錄工具卻未完成。目前先用同一份共享表格。

examples.en: It feels like building the plane while flying it, so one volunteer will maintain the temporary records while we develop the system.
examples.zh: 這感覺像一邊運作一邊建構，所以我們開發系統時，會由一名義工維護臨時紀錄。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出運作與紀錄工具開發重疊，提出一致表格或明確責任；不需聲稱所有準備都沒有。

takeaways.en: The team felt it was building the plane while flying it during the first month.
takeaways.zh: 第一個月，小組覺得像一邊運作一邊建構。

takeaways.en: Building the plane while flying it makes clear temporary procedures especially important.
takeaways.zh: 一邊運作一邊建構，令清楚臨時程序格外重要。

lessons.titleEn: solid ground rather than shifting sand
lessons.titleZh: 穩固根基而非不穩支撐

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Structured training offers solid ground rather than shifting sand.
sources.expression: solid ground rather than shifting sand

brief.meaningEn: Reliable support or clear principles instead of an uncertain basis that keeps changing.
brief.meaningZh: 可靠支援或清楚原則，而非不穩定、不斷改變的基礎。
brief.grammar: offer/provide solid ground rather than shifting sand; extended ground metaphor, not a fixed technical term.
brief.register: Explanatory comparison for learning, planning or support.
brief.boundaryZh: 穩固不是保證永不改變或不用判斷；比喻不評斷真實土地是否安全。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需說明可靠來源，例如清楚訓練或確認資料，而非只因熟悉便說可靠。
brief.outcomeZh: 能比較有依據的支援與不確定假設，並保留更新需要。

options.en: Clear procedures and someone prepared to guide them.
options.zh: 清楚程序及有準備提供指導的人。

options.en: Different informal guesses from whoever happened to be nearby.
options.zh: 碰巧在場的人各自提供不同猜測。

options.en: A decision to leave questions unanswered until the project ended.
options.zh: 決定把問題留到項目結束後才答。

options.en: Advice based only on what had felt familiar years earlier.
options.zh: 只按多年前覺得熟悉的做法提供建議。

listening.explanationZh: 具體書面程序及受訓導師提供可依據的支援，與猜測或過時印象不同。
listening.en: A written procedure and a trained mentor gave the new volunteers solid ground rather than shifting sand when questions arose.
listening.zh: 遇到問題時，書面程序及受訓導師給新義工穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want an agreed guide for new helpers?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想給新幫手一份大家同意的指引？

options.en: They need a reliable place to check the basic steps.
options.zh: 他們需要可靠地方查基本步驟。

options.en: It offers solid ground rather than shifting sand when different people give different advice.
options.zh: 不同人給不同建議時，它提供穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。

options.en: A shared guide can reduce confusion about responsibilities.
options.zh: 共享指引可減少對責任的混亂。

options.en: We can update one clear document instead of passing on rumours.
options.zh: 我們可更新同一份清楚文件，而非傳遞傳聞。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋一致可靠指引的作用；金句以地面比喻比較支援品質。

scene.promptZh: 你要教新同學用設備，可用已確認的操作指引及導師，或靠同學記憶中的不同說法。哪句最貼切地說明前者？

options.en: The guide and mentor offer solid ground rather than shifting sand.
options.zh: 指引和導師提供穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。

options.en: We should rely on whichever unconfirmed instruction we hear first.
options.zh: 我們應靠最先聽到的未確認指示。

options.en: The different memories are a clearer basis than the checked guide.
options.zh: 不同記憶比已確認指引提供更清楚的基礎。

scene.explanationZh: 已確認資料及可請教的人比未確認記憶更可靠，並非聲稱永不用更新。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 solid ground rather than shifting sand 的比喻得出？

options.en: The support has a more reliable basis.
options.zh: 支援有較可靠基礎。

options.en: No future change or checking can ever be necessary.
options.zh: 以後永遠不可能需要更改或核對。

options.en: Clear information can reduce uncertainty.
options.zh: 清楚資料可減少不確定。

contrast.explanationZh: 穩固基礎仍可按新資料更新，並非永久免核對。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「指引可靠，明年換器材也照舊用吧？」哪句較準確？

options.en: It gives us solid ground rather than shifting sand now, but we should review it when the equipment changes.
options.zh: 它現在給我們穩固根基，而非不穩支撐，但換器材時應重新檢視。

options.en: Keep the old steps unchanged and ask new users to work around the differences.
options.zh: 保持舊步驟不變，讓新使用者自行適應差別。

options.en: Remove the guide as soon as one detail needs updating.
options.zh: 只要一個細節要更新，就刪掉整份指引。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可靠是基於適用資料，應更新而非盲用舊版或全盤刪掉。

speaking.en: Clear guidance gives beginners solid ground rather than shifting sand.
speaking.zh: 清楚指導給初學者穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說明可靠指導的作用。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社團報名曾靠口耳相傳，現在你們整理了已確認的步驟及聯絡人，並安排有更改時更新。用一至兩句英文比較新舊支援。

examples.en: The checked guide offers solid ground rather than shifting sand. New members can follow clear steps and contact the organiser with questions.
examples.zh: 已確認指引提供穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。新組員可以跟從清楚步驟，有問題則聯絡主辦者。

examples.en: We want solid ground rather than shifting sand, so we will keep the registration guide clear and update it when arrangements change.
examples.zh: 我們想有穩固根基，而非不穩支撐，所以會保持報名指引清楚，安排改變時便更新。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用已確認指引及聯絡人支持可靠性，並保留安排改變時更新的需要。

takeaways.en: Structured training can provide solid ground rather than shifting sand.
takeaways.zh: 有結構的培訓可提供穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。

takeaways.en: We need solid ground rather than shifting sand when planning the next stage.
takeaways.zh: 規劃下一階段時，我們需要穩固根基，而非不穩支撐。

sources.sentence: Experience gave her a firmer footing in her career.

brief.meaningEn: A more secure position or basis from which to act or develop.
brief.meaningZh: 比以前更穩妥的處境或基礎，讓人可繼續行動和發展。
brief.grammar: give someone/put something on a firmer footing; comparative requires a less secure earlier state.
brief.register: Common balance metaphor in work, learning and planning.
brief.boundaryZh: 較穩固不表示所有困難消失，也不是跟別人競爭必勝；不必涉及腳步。
brief.misconceptionZh: 交代比以前多了甚麼支持，例如經驗、資料或明確安排。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用新增支援解釋較穩妥的起點，並保留下一步工作。

options.en: She had a more secure skills base for the next stage.
options.zh: 她有更穩固的技能基礎，準備下一階段。

options.en: She had already finished every difficult project.
options.zh: 她已完成每個困難項目。

options.en: She had decided to stop practising the basics.
options.zh: 她決定不再練習基本技巧。

options.en: She had less preparation than before learning the methods.
options.zh: 她學方法後，準備反而比以前少。

listening.explanationZh: 學基本方法支持更穩固起點；before she attempted 表示難項目尚未完成。
listening.en: Learning the basic repair methods put her on a firmer footing before she attempted more difficult projects.
listening.zh: 學會基本維修方法，讓她在嘗試較難項目前有更穩固基礎。

reply.promptEn: What difference did the introductory course make?
reply.promptZh: 入門課程帶來甚麼分別？

options.en: I understand the basic tools well enough to begin supervised practice.
options.zh: 我對基本工具的理解足夠開始有指導的練習。

options.en: It gave me a firmer footing for the next stage of training.
options.zh: 它讓我在下一階段培訓有更穩固基礎。

options.en: I can now identify which steps I still need help with.
options.zh: 我現在能辨認哪些步驟仍要幫忙。

options.en: The practical sessions made the instructions less confusing.
options.zh: 實習課令指示不再那麼混亂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明入門課的實際幫助；金句是比較起點，不聲稱精通。

scene.promptZh: 研究小組原先只靠猜測，訪問及核對資料後才較有把握提出建議。哪句合適？

options.en: The evidence puts the proposal on a firmer footing.
options.zh: 證據讓建議有更穩固基礎。

options.en: The interviews replaced evidence with more guesses.
options.zh: 訪問以更多猜測取代證據。

options.en: The proposal was already final before any information was checked.
options.zh: 任何資料核對前，建議已落實。

scene.explanationZh: 訪問及核對令基礎比猜測穩固，不等於未核對已定稿。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 a firmer footing 得出？

options.en: There is a more secure basis than before.
options.zh: 比以前有更穩妥基礎。

options.en: Further work may still be necessary.
options.zh: 仍可能需要進一步工作。

options.en: Every uncertainty and future difficulty has disappeared.
options.zh: 每項不確定及日後困難都已消失。

contrast.explanationZh: 比較穩固不等於絕對無風險或無困難。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「資料較可靠了，下一步是否可以不用查證？」哪句較準確？

options.en: We are on a firmer footing, but we should still check new information as it comes in.
options.zh: 我們有更穩固基礎，但仍應核對新收到的資料。

options.en: Keep using the first findings even when new evidence contradicts them.
options.zh: 即使新證據相反，也一直用最初發現。

options.en: Discard the checked findings because not every question has been answered.
options.zh: 因為不是每個問題都回答了，就棄用已核對的發現。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已有證據可用，同時按新資料檢查，不盲用或全盤否定。

speaking.en: The training gave us a firmer footing, though we still need practice.
speaking.zh: 培訓讓我們有更穩固基礎，但仍要練習。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說明培訓改善起點而非結束學習。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你準備帶新生導覽，走過路線並請有經驗同學核對資料後，比起初有把握，但仍想排練。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: Checking the route and facts gave me a firmer footing. I would still like to rehearse before leading the tour.
examples.zh: 核對路線和資料讓我有更穩固基礎。我帶導覽前仍想排練。

examples.en: I am on a firmer footing now that an experienced student has checked my notes, but another practice run would help.
examples.zh: 有經驗同學核對筆記後，我現在基礎更穩固，但再練一次仍有幫助。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說清比起初多了核對及經驗支援，仍容許排練，不把較穩固說成完全不用準備。

takeaways.en: Reliable evidence puts the argument on a firmer footing.
takeaways.zh: 可靠證據讓論點有更穩固基礎。

takeaways.en: The first course gave her a firmer footing for further study.
takeaways.zh: 首個課程讓她有更穩固基礎繼續學習。

sources.sentence: For beginners, regular practice will sharpen their skills.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: For beginners, regular practice will sharpen their skills.

brief.meaningEn: Improve abilities through focused practice, feedback or use.
brief.meaningZh: 透過有焦點的練習、回饋或運用，提升能力。
brief.grammar: sharpen someone’s skills; skills are metaphorically made sharper like a tool.
brief.register: Common figurative collocation; identify the relevant ability.
brief.boundaryZh: 磨練不等於已精通，也不是只靠重複次數便保證進步；需合適練習及回饋。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是實際磨工具，也不代表必須批評得尖刻才能改善。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把具體練習方法與技能改善連結。

options.en: It helped improve a particular interviewing ability.
options.zh: 它幫助提升一項具體訪問能力。

options.en: It showed that follow-up questions were no longer needed.
options.zh: 它顯示不再需要追問。

options.en: It replaced question practice with memorising the interviewer’s biography.
options.zh: 它以背誦訪問者生平取代練習提問。

options.en: It made the interviews shorter without changing the students’ questioning ability.
options.zh: 它只縮短訪問，沒有改變學生提問能力。

listening.explanationZh: asking clear follow-up questions 指明改善技能，不是取消追問或只改長度。
listening.en: Working on short interviews helped the students sharpen their skills in asking clear follow-up questions.
listening.zh: 做簡短訪問，幫學生磨練清楚追問的技巧。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to help with the school radio interviews?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想協助校園電台訪問？

options.en: I would like more practice asking questions and listening carefully.
options.zh: 我想多練習提問及仔細聆聽。

options.en: It is a chance to sharpen my skills with feedback from the editor.
options.zh: 這是得到編輯回饋、磨練技能的機會。

options.en: I can learn to ask a useful next question when an answer is unclear.
options.zh: 答案不清楚時，我可學習問有用的下一個問題。

options.en: Reviewing the recordings could help me notice where I interrupt.
options.zh: 重聽錄音可幫我發現在哪裏打斷人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明參與訪問的學習理由；金句包含練習及回饋，不保證立即精通。

scene.promptZh: 學生每週練習簡報，導師指出一項可改進處，他下次再有意識地嘗試。哪句合適？

options.en: The sessions help him sharpen his skills.
options.zh: 這些課節幫他磨練技能。

options.en: The sessions replace all opportunities to practise speaking.
options.zh: 這些課節取代所有練習說話的機會。

options.en: He is only collecting comments and never trying the suggestions.
options.zh: 他只是收集評語，從未嘗試建議。

scene.explanationZh: 練習、回饋及下次嘗試形成具體改善過程，不只是收集評語。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 sharpen their skills 得出？

options.en: Their abilities can become more effective with practice.
options.zh: 能力可透過練習變得更有效。

options.en: They must already have mastered every part of the skill.
options.zh: 他們必定已精通技巧的每一部分。

options.en: Focused feedback may guide improvement.
options.zh: 有焦點的回饋可引導改善。

contrast.explanationZh: 磨練是改善過程，不是已全面精通的證明。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我每天重複同一錯誤，也算有效磨練吧？」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: To sharpen your skills, review the error and practise a better method with feedback.
options.zh: 要磨練技能，就檢討錯誤，配合回饋練習較好的方法。

options.en: Repeat the same attempt without checking what caused the error.
options.zh: 不用查錯因，重複同樣嘗試。

options.en: Measure only how many attempts you finish, not whether the method improves.
options.zh: 只數做完多少次，不看方法是否改善。

dialogue.explanationZh: 改善要針對錯因及方法，不只是重複或累積次數。

speaking.en: Regular feedback helps us sharpen our skills rather than repeat the same mistakes.
speaking.zh: 定期回饋幫我們磨練技能，而非重複同樣錯誤。
speaking.promptZh: 你想連結回饋及技能改善。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想提升攝影取景，計劃每週拍同一地方、比較照片，並向老師請教。用一至兩句英文說明練習方法。

examples.en: I will sharpen my skills by comparing photos of the same place each week. My teacher can help me improve the framing.
examples.zh: 我會每週比較同一地方的照片，磨練技能。老師可幫我改善取景。

examples.en: To sharpen my skills, I will review the pictures and ask for feedback on one aspect of the composition.
examples.zh: 為了磨練技能，我會檢視照片，並就構圖的一個方面尋求回饋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出比較、取景或構圖回饋等具體方法，不只說不停重複，也不用聲稱立即精通。

takeaways.en: The workshops helped her sharpen her skills in explaining complex ideas.
takeaways.zh: 工作坊幫她磨練解釋複雜想法的技能。

takeaways.en: We sharpen our skills by practising and reviewing the results.
takeaways.zh: 我們透過練習及檢視成果來磨練技能。

brief.meaningEn: A network of people, roles or opportunities whose activities are interconnected; large and small indicate scale.
brief.meaningZh: 人、角色或機會的活動互相連結、彼此影響的網絡；large 及 small 交代規模。
brief.grammar: an institution can be a large ecosystem of people/ideas/opportunities; a family can work like a small ecosystem, with connected contributions and needs. Large versus small describes scale, while the shared ecosystem metaphor concerns interdependence.
brief.register: Explanatory extension of a biological term; name actual connections rather than size alone.
brief.boundaryZh: 規模不決定成員是否相同或互助是否良好；需有實際連結，本課不指自然生態。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需要互相依賴或交流的具體例子，而不只是很多部門並排存在。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述不同規模群體內有依據的連結、合作及互相支持關係。

options.en: Connections between different people and resources.
options.zh: 不同人及資源之間的連結。

options.en: Departments working separately without exchanging anything.
options.zh: 部門各自工作，完全沒有交流。

options.en: One identical task carried out by every person.
options.zh: 每個人都做同一項完全相同的任務。

options.en: A large building being more important than the links between its users.
options.zh: 大建築物比使用者之間的連結更重要。

listening.explanationZh: shared ideas 提供互相連結的具體線索，不只是一間大建築物。
listening.en: The college was a large ecosystem: students shared ideas with librarians, workshop leaders and local project teams.
listening.zh: 學院是一個互相連結的大網絡：學生與圖書館員、工作坊導師及本地項目團隊交流想法。

reply.promptEn: What do you value about studying at that college?
reply.promptZh: 在那間學院學習，你重視甚麼？

options.en: I can get advice from people in several different departments.
options.zh: 我可以向幾個不同部門的人請教。

options.en: It is a large ecosystem where ideas move between classes and community projects.
options.zh: 它是一個大網絡，想法在課堂與社區項目之間流動。

options.en: The library connects us with workshops we would not have found alone.
options.zh: 圖書館讓我們接觸到自己未必找到的工作坊。

options.en: Working with another course has introduced me to new ways of solving problems.
options.zh: 與另一課程合作，讓我認識解難新方法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均指出學院的人和資源連結；金句不是只談建築或人數。

scene.promptZh: 市集有農夫、廚師、運輸及維修團隊互相合作，大家的工作彼此支持。哪句合適？

options.en: The market functions as a large ecosystem of connected activities.
options.zh: 市集像一個互相連結的大網絡運作。

options.en: The teams work in isolation and have no effect on one another.
options.zh: 各團隊孤立工作，互不影響。

options.en: The only connection is that everyone has exactly the same job.
options.zh: 唯一連結是每個人的工作完全相同。

scene.explanationZh: 不同工作相互支持，才是此處網絡的重點，不要求同職責。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜單憑 a large ecosystem 的機構比喻得出？

options.en: Different groups can affect or support one another.
options.zh: 不同群體可互相影響或支持。

options.en: Size alone guarantees that cooperation works well.
options.zh: 只看規模便能保證合作良好。

options.en: The useful connections should be examined as well as the separate parts.
options.zh: 除了各部分，也應了解有用的連結。

contrast.explanationZh: 大型網絡仍要看實際交流及協調，規模不保證效果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「部門很多，自然就會配合好吧？」哪句較準確？

options.en: A large ecosystem needs working connections, so we should ask how the teams share information.
options.zh: 大網絡需要有效連結，所以應問團隊怎樣共享資訊。

options.en: Count the departments and use that number instead of checking how they cooperate.
options.zh: 數部門數目，用它代替了解合作方式。

options.en: Give every team the same task so there is no need to coordinate different roles.
options.zh: 給每個團隊同一任務，便不用協調不同崗位。

dialogue.explanationZh: 互相連結要有資訊交流及角色配合，不是部門多或職責一樣就足夠。

speaking.en: The university is a large ecosystem of people and ideas that support one another.
speaking.zh: 大學是一個人和想法互相支持的大網絡。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說明機構不同部分的連結。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你參加社區藝術節，圖書館借場地，學生設計海報，工匠帶工作坊，各組互通消息。用一至兩句英文描述這些連結。

examples.en: The festival is a large ecosystem of connected groups. The library, students and craftspeople share resources and information.
examples.zh: 藝術節是一個互相連結的大網絡。圖書館、學生及工匠共享資源和資訊。

examples.en: A large ecosystem supports the festival, with each team contributing different skills and keeping the others informed.
examples.zh: 一個大網絡支持藝術節，各小組貢獻不同技能，並讓其他小組掌握消息。

writing.selfCheckZh: 點名共享資源、不同技能及消息流通，不能只因人多便說互助良好。

takeaways.en: The college forms a large ecosystem of learning and practical support.
takeaways.zh: 學院形成一個學習和實際支援互相連結的大網絡。

takeaways.en: A large ecosystem works better when its teams can share useful information.
takeaways.zh: 大網絡的團隊能共享有用資訊時，運作會更好。

sources.sentence: A doctor's opinion carries a lot of weight in that debate.

sources.sentence: Both suggestions carry some weight in the discussion.

sources.sentence: Course choices can carry real weight for a young person.

sources.sentence: The final decision will carry more weight than a casual suggestion.

sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 232, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Subtle details can carry even more weight among collectors.

brief.meaningEn: Have influence or importance, including the importance of consequential choices. In the main examples here, it concerns persuasive force in a decision or discussion.
brief.meaningZh: 有影響或重要性，也可指帶來後果的選擇之分量。本課主例以決定或討論中的說服力為焦點。
brief.grammar: carry weight / carry even more weight; weight figuratively names significance or persuasive force. Even more explicitly compares the importance with an earlier or alternative detail.
brief.register: Common figurative expression; some/real/more/enormous/a lot of adjust degree without creating a different idiom. A community organiser may tell colleagues that a trusted adviser’s view carries enormous weight with residents.
brief.boundaryZh: 有分量不表示決定由它單獨控制，也不保證內容正確或所有結果已定；本課不是物理承重。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要指出對誰或在哪個判斷中有影響，並容許其他證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明意見或資料的影響程度，而不把影響當成最後保證。

options.en: They treated it as influential while considering other evidence too.
options.zh: 他們認為建議有影響，同時也考慮其他證據。

options.en: They ignored it because experience was irrelevant to the equipment.
options.zh: 他們認為經驗與器材無關，所以忽略建議。

options.en: They accepted it without reading any test results.
options.zh: 他們不看任何測試結果便接受建議。

options.en: They asked her only to record a decision that others had already made.
options.zh: 他們只請她記錄別人已作出的決定。

listening.explanationZh: 經驗令建議有分量，though 後保留其他證據，不是盲從或完全不理會。
listening.en: Her experience with the equipment meant her advice carried weight with the team, though they also checked the test results.
listening.zh: 她有使用器材的經驗，所以建議對小組有分量，但他們也查了測試結果。

reply.promptEn: Why should we listen carefully to the technician’s view?
reply.promptZh: 我們為甚麼應仔細聽技術員的看法？

options.en: She has repaired this model many times and can explain its common faults.
options.zh: 她修過這個型號很多次，能解釋常見故障。

options.en: Her practical experience means her advice carries weight.
options.zh: 她的實際經驗令建議有分量。

options.en: She can connect the test readings with what she has seen before.
options.zh: 她能把測試數據與以前經驗連結。

options.en: Her explanation could help us judge which further checks are useful.
options.zh: 她的解釋可幫我們判斷哪些進一步檢查有用。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明聽取看法的理由；金句是影響力，不是自動作最後決定。

scene.promptZh: 小組在討論活動時間，特別重視輪椅使用者對交通及出入口的第一手經驗。哪句合適？

options.en: Their first-hand experience carries weight in the discussion.
options.zh: 他們的第一手經驗在討論中有分量。

options.en: Their experience is heard only after the time has been fixed.
options.zh: 時間定好後才聽取他們的經驗。

options.en: Their experience has no relevance to accessibility planning.
options.zh: 他們的經驗與無障礙安排無關。

scene.explanationZh: 特別重視相關第一手經驗，支持它在討論中有影響。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句的 carry weight 不是本課「有影響」的意思？

options.en: The safety evidence carries weight with the organisers.
options.zh: 安全證據對主辦方有分量。

options.en: The shelf is designed to carry weight evenly across its supports.
options.zh: 層架的設計讓重量平均分布於支撐點上。

options.en: Her explanation carried weight during the review.
options.zh: 她的解釋在檢討中有分量。

contrast.explanationZh: 層架平均承受重量指物理承重；意見及證據在討論中有分量才是本課比喻。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她的意見有分量，所以可以省掉測試嗎？」哪句較準確？

options.en: Her advice carries weight, but we should compare it with the test evidence before deciding.
options.zh: 她的建議有分量，但決定前應與測試證據比較。

options.en: Use her recommendation first and read the test results only if a problem occurs.
options.zh: 先照她推薦去做，有問題才看測試結果。

options.en: Ask only who supports her view rather than what evidence supports it.
options.zh: 只問誰支持她的看法，不問有甚麼證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 相關經驗值得重視，仍需與證據互相核對；不能以支持者人數代替內容。

speaking.en: The evidence carries weight, but it should be considered alongside the other findings.
speaking.zh: 這項證據有分量，但應與其他發現一併考慮。
speaking.promptZh: 你想承認證據重要而不說它是唯一考慮。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校想改午餐安排，經常使用服務的學生提供具體排隊紀錄。用一至兩句英文說明他們的資料值得重視，並建議與其他回饋比較。

examples.en: The students’ queue records carry weight because they use the service regularly. We should compare them with the staff’s observations.
examples.zh: 學生的排隊紀錄有分量，因為他們經常使用服務。我們應把它們與員工觀察比較。

examples.en: Their first-hand evidence carries weight, but the final plan should also consider other users’ feedback.
examples.zh: 他們的第一手證據有分量，但最終安排也應考慮其他使用者回饋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出實際使用及紀錄讓資料有分量，也保留比較其他回饋；不要說自動決定全部安排。

takeaways.en: A careful explanation can carry weight with people making the decision.
takeaways.zh: 仔細的解釋可對決策者有分量。

takeaways.en: After the cataloguing errors surfaced, the conservator’s notes carried even more weight in the committee’s decision.
takeaways.zh: 編目錯誤曝光後，修復師的筆記對委員會決定更具分量。

sources.sentence: In a small field, reputation often travels ahead of you.
sources.expression: reputation often travels ahead of you

brief.meaningEn: People may know about someone’s past work or behaviour before meeting them.
brief.meaningZh: 別人在見面前，可能已聽過某人過往工作或行為。
brief.grammar: someone’s reputation travels ahead of them; often adds frequency, not a guarantee; travelled in British English.
brief.register: Personification of reputation; can be positive or negative.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示所有人都聽過，也不保證傳聞準確或見面後看法不變。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是本人比自己早到；說的是先前資訊流傳，需要區分聲譽及查證。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述先於見面的印象來源，同時避免把傳聞當定論。

listening.promptZh: 新小組在見面前已有甚麼？

options.en: Information about his past approach to training.
options.zh: 關於他過往培訓方式的資訊。

options.en: Their own experience of working with him in this team.
options.zh: 在這個小組跟他共事的親身經驗。

options.en: A final judgement based on watching his first session there.
options.zh: 看過他在那裏首課後的最終判斷。

options.en: No knowledge of him until after his arrival.
options.zh: 他到達後才開始對他有認識。

listening.explanationZh: had heard before he arrived 說明先聽過往事，不是已親身觀察這次工作。
listening.en: His reputation had travelled ahead of him: the new team had heard about his patient training before he arrived.
listening.zh: 他的聲譽比他本人先被知道：他到達前，新小組已聽過他耐心培訓的事。

reply.promptEn: How did people know about you before your first visit?
reply.promptZh: 你第一次到訪前，大家怎樣已知道你的事？

options.en: A former colleague had shared examples of my work.
options.zh: 前同事曾分享我的工作例子。

options.en: My reputation travelled ahead of me through the local volunteering network.
options.zh: 我的聲譽透過本地義工網絡，比我本人先被知道。

options.en: The organiser had spoken to someone who worked with me before.
options.zh: 主辦者跟以前與我共事的人談過。

options.en: They had read a report about the project I helped run.
options.zh: 他們讀過一篇關於我協辦項目的報道。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均提供見面前的資訊來源；金句把聲譽擬人化，不聲稱人人都認識。

scene.promptZh: 你到新工作坊前，導師已從其他義工聽過你擅長耐心解釋，見面後仍想親自了解。哪句合適？

options.en: Your reputation travelled ahead of you.
options.zh: 你的聲譽比你本人先被知道。

options.en: The tutor formed that impression only after watching you at the new workshop.
options.zh: 導師只在新工作坊看過你後才形成那個印象。

options.en: The tutor knew nothing about your past work before meeting you.
options.zh: 導師見你前，對你過往工作毫不知情。

scene.explanationZh: 先聽過以往做法，符合聲譽先被知道，並不排除再觀察。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 reputation travels ahead of you 得出？

options.en: People may hear about past conduct before a first meeting.
options.zh: 人們可能首次見面前已聽過過往行為。

options.en: Every report about the person must be accurate and complete.
options.zh: 關於那個人的每項傳述必定準確完整。

options.en: Earlier contacts can influence an initial impression.
options.zh: 先前聯繫可以影響初步印象。

contrast.explanationZh: 傳述先到達不保證內容準確完整，仍需核對及觀察。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我先聽過他工作好，就不用再看實際表現了吧？」哪句較準確？

options.en: His reputation travels ahead of him, but we should still get to know how he works here.
options.zh: 他的聲譽比他本人先被知道，但我們仍應了解他在這裏如何工作。

options.en: Assign the most difficult task immediately on the basis of the recommendation alone.
options.zh: 只憑推薦就立即分配最難任務。

options.en: Keep repeating the recommendation instead of asking about the skills this task needs.
options.zh: 一直重複推薦說法，不問這項任務所需技能。

dialogue.explanationZh: 聲譽提供起點，仍需了解當前任務及實際工作，不能以傳述代替觀察。

speaking.en: Your reputation often travels ahead of you, but people still need to know your current work.
speaking.zh: 你的聲譽往往比本人先被知道，但大家仍要了解你現在的工作。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述聲譽的影響及其界線。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你到另一間社區中心幫忙前，負責人已從合作伙伴聽過你組織活動的經驗。你想承認這個印象，同時願意說明這次可做甚麼。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: My reputation travelled ahead of me through our partner centre. I would still like to explain how I can help with this event.
examples.zh: 我的聲譽透過合作中心，比我本人先被知道。我仍想說明這次活動可以怎樣幫忙。

examples.en: It seems my reputation has travelled ahead of me, but let us discuss the tasks and the experience I can offer.
examples.zh: 看來我的聲譽比本人先被知道，但我們還是談談任務及我可提供的經驗吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代合作中心傳述在先，保留討論當前任務；不用說所有人都知道你或傳述必定完整。

takeaways.en: Her reputation travelled ahead of her, so the team knew about her earlier work.
takeaways.zh: 她的聲譽比本人先被知道，所以小組已知道她以前的工作。

takeaways.en: A reputation can travel ahead of you without telling the whole story.
takeaways.zh: 聲譽可比本人先被知道，同時未能交代全部情況。

brief.meaningEn: Begin to become popular or successful quickly.
brief.meaningZh: 開始迅速受歡迎或取得成功。
brief.grammar: a business/idea/event takes off; took off, has taken off; intransitive in this sense.
brief.register: Common figurative phrasal verb; separate from departure or removing clothes.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是單指開業，也不保證長期成功；may take off 表示可能，不能改成一定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需有受歡迎或發展加快的線索，不只因用了新名字便說成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述受歡迎程度開始加快，並區分目前進展及長期結果。

listening.promptZh: took off 描述甚麼變化？

options.en: The club began attracting much more interest and participation.
options.zh: 社團開始吸引更多興趣及參與。

options.en: The club had merely chosen a name without receiving bookings.
options.zh: 社團只是選了名稱，沒有收到預約。

options.en: The bookings stayed unchanged after the videos were shared.
options.zh: 短片分享後，預約維持不變。

options.en: The club stopped holding workshops because interest had fallen.
options.zh: 興趣下降，令社團停止辦工作坊。

listening.explanationZh: bookings rose sharply 是受歡迎程度快速增加的具體證據。
listening.en: The repair club took off after a neighbour shared its workshop videos; bookings rose sharply within two weeks.
listening.zh: 鄰居分享工作坊短片後，維修社迅速受歡迎；兩星期內預約大增。

reply.promptEn: How has the new lunchtime chess club been doing?
reply.promptZh: 新午間棋社近況怎樣？

options.en: More students have joined each week since the first demonstration.
options.zh: 首場示範後，每週加入的學生都增加。

options.en: It has really taken off, and we now need another room.
options.zh: 它真的迅速受歡迎，現在需要多一間房。

options.en: The waiting list has grown faster than we expected.
options.zh: 等候名單增長比預期快。

options.en: The beginners’ sessions are attracting students from several classes.
options.zh: 初學課吸引幾個班的學生。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均回應參與增長；金句不保證未來永遠同樣受歡迎。

scene.promptZh: 社區電影夜原先只有少量觀眾，口碑傳開後每場報名迅速增加。哪句合適？

options.en: The film nights have taken off.
options.zh: 電影夜迅速受歡迎。

options.en: The organisers have only announced the idea and received no response yet.
options.zh: 主辦者只是公布想法，尚未有回應。

options.en: Interest has remained low with no change in attendance.
options.zh: 興趣一直低，出席沒有改變。

scene.explanationZh: 口碑及報名快速增加支持發展加快，不是只公布或維持低參與。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句的 take off 不是本課「迅速受歡迎」的意思？

options.en: The new market took off after local residents recommended it.
options.zh: 本地居民推薦後，新市集迅速受歡迎。

options.en: The plane will take off after the passengers are seated.
options.zh: 乘客坐好後，飛機會起飛。

options.en: The idea has taken off among student volunteers.
options.zh: 這個想法在學生義工之間迅速受歡迎。

contrast.explanationZh: 飛機 take off 是實際起飛；活動或想法受歡迎才是本課意思。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「首月很多人參加，我們可以停止收集回饋嗎？」哪句較合適？

options.en: The club has taken off, but listening to members will help us keep the sessions useful.
options.zh: 社團已迅速受歡迎，但聆聽組員有助課節保持實用。

options.en: Add more sessions immediately without checking why the current ones are popular.
options.zh: 不查現有課節為何受歡迎，就立即加開更多。

options.en: Use the first month’s numbers as the only guide when planning the rest of the year.
options.zh: 規劃全年時，只用首月數字作指引。

dialogue.explanationZh: 起初受歡迎值得肯定，仍需了解原因、回饋及後續需要。

speaking.en: The project has taken off, but we still need to plan the next stage carefully.
speaking.zh: 項目已迅速受歡迎，但下一階段仍須審慎規劃。
speaking.promptZh: 你想報告發展加快，同時保留後續規劃。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：校園交換書本活動開始時只有十人，幾次介紹後，報名快速增加，你想報告進展並查場地容量。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The book exchange has taken off after several introductions. We should check whether the room can hold the growing number of participants.
examples.zh: 幾次介紹後，交換書本活動迅速受歡迎。我們應查房間是否容納得下增加的參加者。

examples.en: The activity took off as more students heard about it, so we need to review the space before adding another session.
examples.zh: 更多學生知道後，活動迅速受歡迎，所以加開活動前要檢視空間。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用報名增加支持受歡迎的變化，提出容量或空間檢查，不保證全年成功。

takeaways.en: The workshop took off after participants shared their experiences.
takeaways.zh: 參加者分享體驗後，工作坊迅速受歡迎。

takeaways.en: An idea can take off quickly and still need careful support.
takeaways.zh: 想法可以迅速受歡迎，同時仍需要細心支援。
